messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: kronecker in Stan
parts:
Hi all. I was speaking with Alex Volfovsky and now I’m all excited again about his hierarchical anova model with Peter Hoff; see here;
http://andrewgelman.com/2013/04/03/hierarchical-array-priors-for-anova-decompositions/
The model uses matrix-normal and array-normal MVN distributions in which the cov matrix is set up as a kronecker product. I recall we had some earlier convos about using kron product in Stan. Anyone interested in this? A possible intermediate solution would be to write a Stan function that implements kron, and if it works we could talk about hardcoding it? What do people think?
See you
A

messages.author: a236d3d356ca53fd
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] kronecker in Stan
parts:
In that Issue
Bob. "Need utilities for Kroneckers for Gaussian processes."

and

bgoodri:
"I think the most immediate need is to have a user-facing function called something like quad_form_kronecker ... Z' * kronecker_product(X, Y) * Z ..."

I think quad_form_kronecker is useful but not enough.
1) For example for many Gaussian process models we have discussed with Andrew, it would be useful to define a list of small covariance matrices K1, K2, K3, ..., KM instead of just X and Y
2) For GPs, instead of quad form (which you could have, too), it would be better to have Cholesky form which can used with (times vector|left division|log trace|multi_normal_cholesky)
3) With MML it would also useful to be able to just define Kronecker product by just listing the small matrices and never forming the full natrix

Aki

[off users list]

We should be having this discussion on stab-dev.  Seth — would you like
me to give you permissions to post there (assuming you are already
subscribed).

Andrew:   We have no mechanism by which to distribute something written
as a Stan function.  We need to figure out includes first.  

The big bottleneck to getting things into Stan is the testing and doc.

Seth  1:  Yes, there’s issues in sparse structures.  There’s better support
in Eigen now.  It’s a pretty major overhaul as it’ll need a design for how to
declare such a structure, then changes to the parser, abstract syntax
tree, code generator, and all the I/O.  Then it’ll percolate through R and
Python and MATLAB and Julia.

Seth 2:  It’d be great if you help us design what we’ll need.

- Bob

messages.author: a236d3d356ca53fd
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: [stan-dev] kronecker in Stan
parts:
It would be nice to have a Kronecker and sparse matrix data types. Then the rest of the Stan code for some model would be same, for example, if the type of covariance matrix is changed (naturally the code constructing the matrix would be different for a Kronecker product matrix).

First you could start by defining the Kronecker data type, but inside functions just compute the corresponding full matrix and then use the normal function. Then you could start modifying functions which can exploit the Kronecker form.

An alternative approach is to have just couple helper functions in Stan language to form Kronecker products and compute quadratic forms etc.

Aki

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Stan functions somewhere that are accessible
parts:
Sure. We could put it in example-models or we could
create a new public repo called something like stan-functions.
Let’s decide on naming and repo organization and vetting process
for contribs (if any) at the meeting tomorrow.

The drawback for users is that they have to cut-and-paste
them into our models until we get includes sorted out. Then
we could distribute a library of such functions.

The drawback for developers is that we don’t have a good way
of testing Stan functions.

Both of these issues are fairly high priorities for us.

- Bob
